title: Terminate SubD density with convex 2-to-1 quad flow
preconditions: extra density should terminate on a low-curvature or visually quiet region
the reduction can preserve one connected quad surface
the evaluated result can be inspected under curvature rather than only while flat
required_observations: fixed MatCap after Bend or equivalent curvature
action_policy: Route the denser boundary into the coarser boundary with convex quads whose corners remain outward.
Ease polygon size across the reduction; do not place the reduction vertex behind the incoming boundary or create an inward-folding concave quad.
Place the reduction away from a critical corner when possible, then evaluate it on the intended curved surface with the real modifier stack.
expected_effects: no concentrated fan or crease in evaluated wire/MatCap
failure_predicates: any reduction quad becomes concave or self-overlapping
wire converges into a concentrated fan
MatCap shows a localized crease despite matched counts and modifiers
recovery: move the reduction vertex back inside the convex transition region
spread the size change across more than one row
relocate the reduction to a flatter region

sources.description: Ryuu - Blender Bros demonstrates loop termination, rejects an inward-folding diamond, and eases polygon size.

experiments.limitations: One reduction family under one Bend/Solidify/SubD stack. Candidate counts do not identify the defect; the result depends on wire and MatCap judgment and still needs transfer to a different curved asset.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS reproduction; source tutorial used Blender 3.6
status_note: Matched reproduction isolates convexity as the visual difference; different-geometry transfer and complete-asset use remain open.
